entries.name: Check
paragraphs: `CHECK RETOOLS` displays the outstanding item retools handled by the retool-certification NPC. Each entry identifies the affected item and its proposed text changes.

This is a staff review command that works only at the appropriate NPC. Read the proposed names and descriptions before using the certification instructions shown there. `CHECK` by itself is not a general-purpose item inspection command; use `LOOK` or `EXAMINE` for that.

entries.name: Compact
paragraphs: `COMPACT` toggles the extra blank line normally printed before your prompt. Turn it on to fit more game output on the screen; type it again to restore the spacing.
This changes prompt spacing only. Use `BRIEF` to control room descriptions and `TOGGLE` to review your other preferences.

entries.name: Enter
paragraphs: `ENTER` attempts to take you through an entrance in your current room. Specify the entrance keyword when the room provides one. With no argument, it looks for an open exit leading indoors.

Some entrances have their own requirements, such as an unlocked door, permission from a guard, or progress in a quest. Read the room description for the appropriate keyword. `ENTER ARENA` instead requests entry to the Arena queue or match.

entries.name: Equipment
paragraphs: `EQUIPMENT` lists the items you currently have equipped, including your weapon, armor, held item, and light source. Each item appears beside the slot it occupies.

Items you are carrying but have not equipped appear under `INVENTORY`. Use `WEAR`, `WIELD`, or `HOLD` to equip an item, and `REMOVE` to put equipped items back into your inventory. The usual abbreviation for this command is `EQ`.

entries.name: Examine
paragraphs: `EXAMINE` takes a closer look at a visible target. Examining a container also shows its accessible contents; a closed container may need to be opened first.

Some weapons, armor, recipe fragments, and other special items provide additional information when examined. What you can learn depends on the item. Use the target keywords shown by `LOOK` or `INVENTORY`.

entries.name: Fade
paragraphs: `FADE` allows a Myrddraal to travel through the shadows to a room identified by its fading code. Use `SENSE DARKNESS` in a suitable room to learn its code for a future journey.

You must be unmounted and in a dark room that permits shadow travel. Your Fade skill affects the attempt and how far you can travel. The journey uses shadow strength; protected or inaccessible destinations cannot be reached this way.

entries.name: Get
paragraphs: `GET` picks up an item from the ground or removes it from a container. Leave out the container name to take something from your room. The item must be visible and available to take, and you must have enough carrying capacity.

Use `ALL` to take all eligible items, or `ALL.KEYWORD` to take items sharing a keyword. A numbered keyword such as `2.sword` selects a particular matching item. Closed containers must be opened first. `TAKE` is another name for this command.

entries.name: Give
paragraphs: `GIVE` hands an item from your inventory to a visible character in your room. The recipient must be able to carry it. Remove an equipped item before giving it away.

You can also transfer money by specifying an amount and the word `COINS`. Giving an item or money to an NPC may trigger a purchase, quest, or other interaction, so check that you have selected the intended recipient.

entries.name: Group
paragraphs: `GROUP` with no argument displays your group. As the leader, use `GROUP <NAME>` to include a character who is following you and standing in your room. Repeating it for an existing member removes that character from the group.

`GROUP ALL` adds eligible followers. Following and group membership are separate: `FOLLOW` establishes who leads, while `GROUP` decides who belongs to the party. A character following someone else cannot enroll their own group members.

entries.name: Guilds
paragraphs: `GUILDS` opens the guild interface. Use its menu to browse guild information and the membership or management options available to your character.

The interface determines which actions you may take from your membership, rank, and privileges. Follow the menu prompts and use its exit option when finished. Guilds use a separate interface from the clan commands.

entries.name: Hamstring
paragraphs: `HAMSTRING` is a Blademaster technique that attempts to wound an opponent and reduce their ability to dodge. You must know the Hamstring skill and use an appropriate sword.
Specify a visible target in your room, or omit the name to use your current opponent. The attack takes time to prepare and may miss. A target flying out of reach cannot be hamstrung.

entries.name: Invert
paragraphs: `INVERT` prepares your next weave to be inverted. You must know the Invert weave and already be connected to the True Source through `EMBRACE` or `SEIZE`.

A successful preparation costs spell points. Being shielded prevents the attempt, and loss of concentration can cause it to fail. You cannot prepare another inversion while one is already waiting for your next weave.

entries.name: Kill
paragraphs: `KILL` starts ordinary combat against a visible target in your room. The target must be within reach, and the room must permit fighting. For ordinary players this is an attack command, not an instant kill.
`ATTACK` is an alias for this command. Once combat begins, your character continues making normal attacks. Use `ASSIST` to join an ally against their opponent, or `FLEE` to attempt to escape.

entries.name: Knock
paragraphs: `KNOCK` announces your presence at a door. Use the door keyword from the room description; a direction can distinguish doors with the same keyword.

Knocking does not itself unlock or open an ordinary door. Some clan entrances have guards or special responses that decide whether you may enter. Wait for the response and follow any instructions given.

entries.name: Lead
paragraphs: `LEAD` attempts to make an available mount in your room follow you. Your Ride skill affects whether the animal cooperates. Mounts already ridden or following someone else cannot simply be taken over.

The mount must be suitable for your character. Leading keeps it travelling with you on foot; use `RIDE` to mount it and `DISMOUNT` to get down. Leading a mount does not automatically put another player into a group.

entries.name: Levels
paragraphs: `LEVELS` lists how much experience is required to advance from each level to the next. These are individual advancement costs, not cumulative experience totals. Consult the list when planning your next advancement.
This command displays information only; it does not grant experience or change your level. Use `SCORE` to review your own character and `PRACTICE` to check your training.

entries.name: Lock
paragraphs: `LOCK` secures a closed door or container that has a lock. You must have the correct key available. Close an open door or container before trying to lock it.

Use the door or item keyword, adding a direction for a door when needed to distinguish it. Some locks are controlled by guards or special interactions instead of ordinary keys. Use `UNLOCK` to open a lock you have secured.

entries.name: Mark
paragraphs: `MARK` lets a greyman focus on a visible character in the same room. A successful mark replaces the character you were previously focusing on.
This is a greyman ability rather than an item-marking command. Choose the target by name. Marking someone does not itself strike them or move you to their location.

entries.name: Open
paragraphs: `OPEN` opens a door or container that can be opened. Use its keyword, and add a direction when you need to distinguish between similarly named doors.

A locked target must first be unlocked or opened through the appropriate special interaction. Opening a container makes its contents accessible; it does not pick them up. Use `GET` to take items from it and `CLOSE` when finished.

entries.name: Order
paragraphs: `ORDER` instructs a character under your control to carry out a command. The recipient must be in your room and obey you; an ordinary player following you is not forced to comply.

Use `FOLLOWERS` to address your eligible followers together. Orders are subject to the follower's normal restrictions and abilities. Giving an order does not guarantee that the requested action can succeed.

entries.name: Pour
paragraphs: `POUR` transfers liquid between suitable containers. The source must contain liquid and the destination must be able to accept it. Existing contents and the destination's capacity may limit what can be transferred.
Use `OUT` as the destination to empty the source onto the ground. This discards the liquid. Oil can also be used to refill a suitable refillable light. Check both item names before pouring.

entries.name: Practice
paragraphs: `PRACTICE` with no argument lists your skills and remaining training sessions. At a suitable trainer, name the skill or weave you want to improve.

Trainers teach particular subjects and have their own limits. You need the appropriate practice sessions, and any other requirements the trainer imposes. Away from a trainer, the command displays your skills rather than teaching a new one.

entries.name: Precisestrike
paragraphs: `PRECISESTRIKE` attempts a carefully aimed weapon attack. You must know the skill and wield a weapon. You may specify a target and body part; while fighting, you can omit the target to use your current opponent.

The chosen body part must be valid. The target must remain visible and in reach while the attack prepares, and success is not guaranteed. You cannot use this technique to attack someone else while already engaged with an unrelated opponent.

entries.name: Pulverize
paragraphs: `PULVERIZE` is an Ogier combat technique. After preparing the attack, you attempt to strike opponents who are fighting you or whom you are fighting.
You must know Pulverize and wait for its cooldown before using it again. The attempt can fail. It takes no target argument; its combat targets are selected from the fighting around you.

entries.name: Quaff
paragraphs: `QUAFF` is a reserved item command. In the current game it has no general potion-drinking effect: specifying an ordinary item does not consume it or apply a potion effect.

Follow the instructions for the particular item you are trying to use. `USE` works only on items that explicitly support it. Typing `QUAFF` alone asks which item you mean, but that prompt does not mean that every potion can be quaffed.

entries.name: Rage
paragraphs: `RAGE` lets a Myrddraal with the Shadow Rage skill draw on dark power to enhance attack speed. Type it again to release the effect.
You need sufficient shadow strength to begin. Watch your condition while using shadow abilities, and turn Rage off when you no longer want the enhancement. This command takes no target argument.

entries.name: Read
paragraphs: `READ` examines written material or another visible target. Its basic behavior uses the same viewing action as `LOOK`; books, notices, recipes, and quest items may provide their own text or interaction.
Use an item or feature keyword from your inventory or the room description. Reading a recipe is different from learning it: use `LEARN` when you want to add an eligible recipe to your recipe book.

entries.name: Release
paragraphs: `RELEASE` ends your connection to the One Power. Use it after `EMBRACE` or `SEIZE` when you no longer want to remain connected to the True Source.

It does not spend practice sessions or remove your learned weaves. To channel again, reconnect to the Source. In certain quests, `RELEASE <CRATE>` is a separate instruction for letting go of a crate you are dragging.

entries.name: Reply
paragraphs: `REPLY` sends a private tell to the player who most recently sent you one. The recipient must still be online and able to receive your tell.

Check who last contacted you before replying: another incoming tell can change the recipient. Use `TELL <NAME> <MESSAGE>` when you want to choose the recipient explicitly. `TELLS` reviews your received tell history.
examples: reply I will meet you at the gate.

entries.name: Rescue
paragraphs: `RESCUE` attempts to draw an attacker away from an ally in your room and onto you. You must know the Rescue skill, and the ally must have an attacker you can take over. The ally must be of your race; you cannot rescue yourself or your opponent.

A successful rescue makes you the attacker's opponent; you should be ready to withstand the fight. The attempt can fail. Use `ASSIST` when you want to attack alongside your ally rather than pull an opponent off them.

entries.name: Rest
paragraphs: `REST` settles your character into a resting position. Resting allows you to recover between journeys and battles, but you cannot move normally until you stand again.
You cannot simply lie down in the middle of a fight. Use `STAND` when you are ready to continue, or `SLEEP` if you want to sleep. Sleeping makes you less aware of activity around you than resting.

entries.name: Restat
paragraphs: `RESTAT` rerolls your character's statistics. This command is available only while you are exactly level five.

Using it immediately changes your statistics; it is not a preview. The new result may differ from the one you had before. Review your character afterwards with `SCORE`. Once you advance beyond level five, this command is no longer available.

entries.name: Scan
paragraphs: `SCAN` looks for visible characters beyond your current room. With a direction, it examines that way; without one, it scans the available directions.

You must be on your feet. Closed doors, darkness, visibility, and the available exits limit what you can see. Some characters need time to complete a scan, so wait for the result before issuing another action. `SCAN` does not reveal every hidden character or room.

entries.name: Search
paragraphs: `SEARCH` examines a direction for a hidden way, or looks for a concealed item by keyword in your current room. Read the room description for clues before choosing what to search.

Finding a hidden item can place it in your inventory if you can carry it. Directional searches depend on the exit and your ability to discover it. Some quest features have their own search responses. This is different from `SCAN`, which looks for visible characters beyond the room.

entries.name: Seize
paragraphs: `SEIZE` allows a male channeler to take hold of the One Power. You must connect to the True Source before channeling weaves.
Access can be prevented by a shield or a location where channeling is blocked. Use `RELEASE` to let go when finished. Female channelers use `EMBRACE` for their connection instead.

entries.name: Sense
paragraphs: `SENSE DARKNESS` allows a Myrddraal to identify a dark room's fading code. Keep the code if you want to attempt to return using `FADE`.

The room must be dark and permit shadow travel. A room with no suitable shadows will not provide a usable result. Sensing a code does not transport you; fading is a separate action with its own range and resource requirements.

entries.name: Shadowstep
paragraphs: `SHADOWSTEP` allows a greyman to slip through the shadows and engage a visible target in the same room. Specify the target by name.

The target must remain within reach; a flying opponent cannot be reached this way. Shadowstepping adds to your flee lag. It does not teleport you to a distant room or automatically kill the target. The current command requires a target.

entries.name: Show
paragraphs: `SHOW` lets a visible character in your room inspect an item you are carrying or wearing. The item stays with you; showing it is not the same as giving it away.
Use an item keyword and the recipient's name. Both must be visible to you. If you intend to transfer ownership instead, remove the item from your equipment if necessary and use `GIVE`.

entries.name: Sip
paragraphs: `SIP` takes a small taste of liquid from an appropriate container or fountain. It consumes less liquid than taking a full drink.

The source must be available and contain liquid. Check its contents before using it, particularly when the origin is uncertain. Use the normal drinking command when you want to drink more, or `POUR` to transfer or discard a container's contents.

entries.name: Skin
paragraphs: `SKIN` removes a usable skin from a suitable corpse. Wield a short blade and have enough Skinning skill for that creature. Not every corpse provides a skin, and a corpse can be skinned only once.
The skin goes into your inventory if you have room and can carry its weight; otherwise it falls to the ground. `BUTCHER` obtains meat instead. Keep useful hides for crafting.

entries.name: Steal
paragraphs: `STEAL` attempts to take an item or money from another character in your room. It is a skill-based attempt rather than a guaranteed transfer.

An unsuccessful attempt may expose you and provoke a response. You cannot steal from yourself, and peaceful rooms prevent the action. Specify the intended item and target carefully; use `GET` for items lying on the ground.

entries.name: Take
paragraphs: `TAKE` is another name for `GET`. It picks up an eligible item from the ground or takes it from the container you specify.
You must be able to see and carry the item. Open a closed container first. Use `ALL` for all eligible items or `ALL.KEYWORD` for matching items. Taking an item does not equip it.

entries.name: Ungroup
paragraphs: `UNGROUP <MEMBER>` removes one of your followers from your group. The member must be in your room. Only the group leader can remove members this way.

Removing a named member leaves that character following you. With no argument, the leader disbands the group and the grouped followers stop following. Use `FOLLOW SELF` when you want to end your own follow relationship.

entries.name: Untie
paragraphs: `UNTIE` lists the gates currently tied to you. To release one, specify `GATE` and its number from that list; use `ALL` to release all of your tied gates.
Releasing a gate affects the passage it provides, so make sure your companions have finished using it. This command manages gates, not ropes, clothing, or mounts.

entries.name: Use
paragraphs: `USE` activates certain special items that you are carrying or have equipped. The effect depends on the item being used.
Only items that specifically support this command respond to it. For example, `USE ROD` attempts to activate a suitable rod in your possession. An unsupported item may produce no response.
Look at an item and follow any instructions provided to learn how to activate it. Food, drink containers, and other ordinary items have their own commands.

entries.name: Whirlwind
paragraphs: `WHIRLWIND` is a Blademaster sword technique that attempts to strike opponents engaged with you. You must know the skill, be fighting, and be unmounted.
The technique takes time to prepare and can fail. It selects opponents from the combat around you rather than taking a target name. Use an appropriate sword and remain ready for the return attacks.

entries.name: Achat
paragraphs: `ACHAT` sends a message to the Arena audience. You must be playing, watching, or queued for an Arena match to use the channel.
Use it for match-wide conversation. Messages are not limited to your teammates; use `TCHAT` for team communication. `ARENA` shows the current Arena status and available options.

entries.name: Achievement
paragraphs: `ACHIEVEMENT MESSAGES` toggles the notifications shown when you unlock achievements or titles. The command reports whether those messages are now on or off.
This preference changes notifications, not your earned achievements. Use the full two-word command; `ACHIEVEMENT` alone does not toggle the setting.

entries.name: Arena
paragraphs: `ARENA` displays information about the Arena and your current match or queue. Use `ARENA HELP` for the complete set of options available in the Arena interface.

`ENTER ARENA` joins the queue or returns you to an eligible match. `EXIT ARENA` leaves; leaving a match early can affect your score. `ARENA WATCH` toggles spectating, while `ARENA RANKS` and `ARENA LEGENDS` display rankings.
During team games, the interface provides team choices and match-specific instructions. `ACHAT` speaks to the Arena audience; `TCHAT` speaks to your team.

entries.name: Capture
paragraphs: `CAPTURE` interacts with capture objectives in Arena games, including eligible towers and flags. You must be standing and at an appropriate objective for the current game.

Name the target identified by the match or room. The result depends on the game mode, your team, and whether you are carrying a flag. It is not a command for taking ownership of ordinary rooms; manor ownership uses `CLAIM`.

entries.name: Combine
paragraphs: `COMBINE` joins matching recipe fragments in your inventory. It looks for fragments belonging to the same recipe and combines their information where possible.

The command takes no item argument. Examine the resulting parchment to check your progress. Once you have an eligible complete recipe, use `LEARN` to add it to your recipe book; `RECIPES` displays the recipes you know.

entries.name: Fish
paragraphs: `FISH` casts a line at a suitable fishing location. You must be at least level five, know Fishing, be standing, and wield an appropriate fishing pole.

Fishing continues over time and can produce different catches. An unsuitable or crowded spot prevents you from starting. Stay at your spot and follow the game's messages; other actions may interrupt the activity.

entries.name: Gather
paragraphs: `GATHER` attempts to harvest a plant from a suitable location using Herbalism. You must be standing and there must be something available to gather.

Use `GATHER PLANT` or `GATHER HERB`. Harvesting takes time, and poor technique may ruin the plant. Successful gathering adds the harvested ingredient to your supplies. Individual quest plants can have their own gathering instructions.

entries.name: Help
paragraphs: `HELP` opens the guide at its Table of Contents. Select a numbered topic, use `B` to go back, or `C` to close the guide.

To open a topic directly, type `HELP` followed by its keyword, such as `HELP GET`. Topic searches use the complete help keyword, so a command abbreviation may not be a help keyword. Pages restricted to higher levels are unavailable until you meet their requirements.
The web client's help navigator uses the same help articles and access restrictions.

entries.name: Journal
paragraphs: `JOURNAL` opens your quest journal. Use its menu to browse recorded quests and review their tasks, progress, and quest-giver information.

You must be standing, sitting, or resting to read it. Enter `JOURNAL` without extra words, then follow the displayed navigation prompts. Quest items kept separately from normal equipment can be inspected with `QI`.

entries.name: Mix
paragraphs: `MIX VIAL` attempts to combine the ingredients in a small mixing vial. Carry the appropriate vial and put the intended ingredients inside it before beginning.

The vial must be filled as required, and everything inside must be a valid mixing ingredient. Your Mixing skill must meet the recipe's requirement. An incorrect mixture can spoil the contents, so check the recipe before starting.

entries.name: Prepare
paragraphs: `PREPARE` converts suitable supplies into materials for Tailoring. You must be at a workshop, with the appropriate skill and enough supplies for the material you request.

Some preparations break down existing items. When the game lists items to be destroyed and asks for confirmation, review that list before answering. Preparation takes time, and interruption can waste materials. Use `TAILOR` to see what you can make and `RECIPES` to review requirements.

entries.name: Quest Inventory
paragraphs: `QI` displays your quest inventory: special quest items tracked separately from your normal inventory. Each entry shows the item name and, where applicable, its quantity.

An empty list means no quest items are currently recorded there. Use `INVENTORY` for ordinary carried objects and `JOURNAL` for quest progress. Use the working command `QI`; the full spelling `QINVENTORY` is not currently registered as an input command.

entries.name: Recall
paragraphs: `RECALL` lets a manor owner or permitted defender attempt to return to a property that is being claimed. It is an emergency manor-defense action, not a general return-to-town command.

You must own or be allowed at the threatened property, and it must have the required portal service. If no eligible property is under claim, the command has no destination. Follow the messages explaining any additional restrictions.

entries.name: Recipes
paragraphs: `RECIPES` opens your recipe book. Its menu groups known recipes by Smithing, Mixing, and Tailoring and also offers a combined list.

Choose a numbered category and recipe to inspect its requirements. Use `C` to close the book. An empty book means you must learn recipes first; fragments may need to be combined before they can be learned. Read the book while out of combat.

entries.name: Report
paragraphs: `REPORT` displays information about the manor you own, including its location, upkeep, and the players you have permitted to enter.

Use it to review ownership and access before changing permissions or buying upkeep. If you do not own a property, the command reports that instead. `ALLOW` changes access, and `RECALL` may help you defend a property under claim.

entries.name: Shoot
paragraphs: `SHOOT` fires a wielded bow at an eligible visible target. Name an opponent in your room, or specify a direction when attempting a shot into an adjacent room. You need the appropriate bow and Bow skill.
Target visibility, closed doors, your position, and the bow's restrictions affect the shot. A target may move or a door may close while you aim. `BARRAGE` is a separate bow technique for an area.
At a ship's cannon, `SHOOT CANNON` instead fires a loaded cannon. That interaction uses cannon ammunition and the ship's firing position, not your bow.

entries.name: Summon
paragraphs: `SUMMON` calls back the mount associated with a Myrddraal or Dreadlord. It is a mount ability; it does not summon arbitrary creatures or other players.

You must have an associated living mount and a Ride skill level of at least five. Summoning takes time and requires the appropriate energy for your class. If the attempt is interrupted or its requirements are not met, the mount will not arrive.

entries.name: Tailor
paragraphs: `TAILOR` with no arguments lists the materials and armor types available at your Tailoring skill. Use those displayed names to request an item.
Crafting requires a workshop, a held tailor's needle, knowledge of the recipe, and enough prepared material. Check `RECIPES` before beginning. The work takes several stages and may be interrupted.
Some heavy or combination-armor options are unfinished and will say so. Only the combinations supported by the current workshop and recipe system can be made.

entries.name: Tchat
paragraphs: `TCHAT` sends a message to your current Arena team. You must belong to a team for it to have recipients.

Use team chat to coordinate positions and objectives without sending the message to the entire Arena audience. Outside a team, the game explains that you cannot use the channel. Use `ACHAT` for Arena-wide conversation.

entries.name: Tells
paragraphs: `TELLS` shows your received tell history, newest first. With no arguments it requests the latest 25 tells. Each line includes a timestamp, sender, and message as permitted by visibility rules.

The first number chooses how many messages to display, up to 100. The second skips that many newest messages, letting you read older entries. Use nonnegative numbers. This reviews incoming messages; it does not send a tell.

entries.name: Throw
paragraphs: `THROW` hurls your wielded throwing weapon at an opponent. Suitable weapons include short blades and eligible one-handed spears or axes. Projectiles and the relevant weapon skill influence the attack.

Name a visible opponent in your room, or use your current opponent while fighting. The weapon leaves your hand, so be prepared to retrieve it or equip another weapon. An unsupported weapon cannot be thrown this way.

entries.name: Tokens
paragraphs: `TOKENS` lists the special tokens recorded for your character and the quantity of each. If you have not gathered any, the command says so.
This is an information display, not an exchange command. Token uses depend on the NPC or event that accepts them. Ordinary items in your pack are listed by `INVENTORY` instead.

entries.name: Tutorial
paragraphs: `TUTORIAL` offers the introductory tutorial to a human character who has not completed it and is still below level five.

You cannot enter while affected by No Quit. Answer the confirmation prompt to begin, then follow the tutorial's instructions. Characters who are too experienced, are not human, or have already completed it cannot start again through this command.

entries.name: Whistle
paragraphs: `WHISTLE` calls the living mount associated with your character, provided your Ride skill level is at least five. The mount attempts to travel to you through the rooms between you.

A closed door or an unavailable route can stop its approach, so whistling does not guarantee arrival. This mount-calling behavior is separate from simply performing a social whistle. Myrddraal and Dreadlords can also have access to `SUMMON`.

entries.name: Who
paragraphs: `WHO` lists connected characters whose information you are allowed to see. The display can include their titles and other public details.

Visibility, race, incognito settings, and immortal privileges can affect the entries. The list is not a locator for every hidden character. Use `WHOIS <NAME>` for information about a particular character and `WHERE` for location information available to you.

entries.name: Whois
paragraphs: `WHOIS` displays the public character information available for a named player. Enter one character name after the command.

The result respects incognito and level-based visibility, so not every field is shown to every viewer. This command does not change the character or locate them in a room. Use `WHO` to review the connected-player list.

entries.name: Ban
entries.syntax: ban [all | select | new | name] [site or name]
paragraphs: `BAN` with no arguments displays the ban list. To add a restriction, specify the ban type and site pattern or character name.

`ALL` blocks matching sites, `NEW` restricts new characters, and `SELECT` allows only approved characters from matching sites. `NAME` reserves the specified character name. Choose the narrowest pattern that covers the intended restriction.
A pattern already on the list must be unbanned before its type is changed. Review the list after editing it.

entries.name: Council
paragraphs: `COUNCIL` toggles council status for a player in a clan. The player must already belong to the clan you specify.

Using it for a council member removes that status; using it for another member grants it. Read the confirmation carefully before repeating the command. It does not add the player to the clan or set their numeric rank.

entries.name: Enable
entries.syntax: enable command global <command> | enable command user <player> <command>
paragraphs: `ENABLE` removes a command restriction previously applied through `DISABLE`. Choose `GLOBAL` for a server-wide restriction or `USER` for one character.

The user form can apply to a character who is offline. Enabling a command removes that restriction only; the character must still satisfy the command's normal level, class, skill, and position requirements.

entries.name: Helpedit
paragraphs: `HELPEDIT` opens the in-game help editor. Use the menus to create and organize topics and edit their name, keywords, syntax, description, and minimum level.
Finish any other editor before opening it. Descriptions use the help system's formatting expressions; preview a page before publishing it. Use comma-separated keywords so `HELP <TOPIC>` can find it.
A page's minimum level also restricts its descendants. Place staff documentation beneath the immortal section and verify its minimum level before saving.

entries.name: Jslist
paragraphs: `JSLIST` lists JavaScript triggers by vnum and name within a numeric range. `JSLIST LIB` requests the negative-vnum range used for library entries.
This lists registered triggers, not every file on the filesystem and not every object carrying an attachment. Use `JSTAT` to inspect a trigger and `JATTACH` for attachment work.

entries.name: Oedit
paragraphs: `OEDIT` opens the online editor for an object prototype. Enter the prototype vnum, then follow the menu to edit its names, descriptions, type, values, flags, and other properties.

Zone permissions and editor locks still apply. Editing a prototype is different from retooling one carried item, and existing loaded items are not necessarily updated by a prototype edit. Save the changes through the editor and the appropriate OLC save workflow.

entries.name: Olc
paragraphs: `OLC` displays the online-creation save information, including areas with changes awaiting persistence. It is a status command rather than a replacement for the room, object, mobile, or shop editors.
Use the appropriate editor for the entity you want to change. Review pending work before using a broad save command; a global save may include other builders' changes.

entries.name: Olist
paragraphs: `OLIST` lists object prototypes by vnum range or item category, such as swords, daggers, weapons, or armor. It displays prototype statistics, not the current contents of a room or inventory. Use `VNUM` for a search by item name.

A numeric range may be followed by a supported sort such as weight, ob, pb, db, or abs. Availability of particular statistics depends on the object type. Use `OLIST` without arguments to review the command's syntax and `VSTAT OBJ` for a specific prototype.

entries.name: Qval
paragraphs: `QVAL` changes a player's stored quest variable. Surround the entire variable name with single quotes. A number by itself is added to the existing value; `SET` assigns an absolute value.

This is a direct state edit, not a quest-completion command. Know the exact variable and expected value before changing it, because quest stages and completion hooks may require other actions as well.

entries.name: Redit
paragraphs: `REDIT` opens the online room editor. Specify a room vnum or use the current room when the editor permits the no-argument form.

The menu controls room text, exits, flags, and other room properties. Zone editing permissions and locks still apply. Check exit destinations and door settings before saving, particularly when changing links used by players or mobile movement.

entries.name: Saveall
paragraphs: `SAVEALL` writes the selected category of world data to persistent storage. `OLC` saves all supported OLC categories.

This is a broad administrative save and can include changes made by other builders. Review pending work with `OLC` and coordinate shared editing before saving. Saving world prototypes is different from saving a player character.

entries.name: Sedit
paragraphs: `SEDIT` opens the online shop editor for a shop vnum. Follow the menu to edit the keeper, trading rules, stock, rooms, and other shop settings.

The shop must be in an area you are permitted to edit, and another builder may already hold its editor lock. Verify the shopkeeper and room references before saving. A shop vnum is not necessarily the keeper's mobile vnum.

entries.name: Set
paragraphs: `SET` changes a supported character field. Without a selector it searches for a target in the game. `PLAYER` and `MOB` limit the target type; `FILE` edits a saved player record.

Use `SET` without enough arguments to display the available fields. Individual fields have their own level, target-type, and value restrictions. A successful edit changes state immediately, so verify the target and original value before applying it.

entries.name: Testroll
paragraphs: `TESTROLL` runs repeated combat-roll simulations and reports their success rate. Supported combat tests include bash, charge, melee, backstab, and precisestrike. Both named characters must be available.

Use a modest count while investigating. The optional `YES` requests individual roll output; omit it or use `NO` for a summary. The separate statistics form is `TESTROLL STATS <COUNT> <GENDER> <RACE> <CLASS> <SHOW?>`.
The command requires the configured stat-editor permission unless you are level 104 or higher. A successful simulation is not a guarantee of an identical outcome in live combat.

entries.name: Unban
paragraphs: `UNBAN` removes a matching entry from the ban list. First use `BAN` to inspect the stored entry and identify the exact site pattern or name you intend to remove.

Removing a restriction allows connections or character names previously blocked by that entry, subject to any other restrictions still in place. To change an entry's ban type, remove it and then add the corrected entry.

entries.name: Vnum
entries.syntax: vnum <obj | mob | kit | room | js | zone> <keyword>
paragraphs: `VNUM` searches world definitions by name and displays their virtual numbers. Select the type of definition and the keyword to find.

Use the resulting vnum with the appropriate editor or inspection command. A prototype search does not tell you where every live instance is currently located. Use a more specific keyword if the results are too broad.

entries.name: Wshow
paragraphs: `WSHOW` displays administrative information. With no arguments it lists the topics available at your level; select a topic and supply the arguments it requires.

Topics include world and zone information and other staff reports. Access can differ between topics even after you can use `WSHOW` itself. Consult the displayed syntax rather than assuming every topic takes a player name.

entries.name: Quedit
paragraphs: `QUEDIT` opens the quest editor. Use its menus to browse existing quests and edit their description, requirements, tasks, dialogue, rewards, and related settings.

Finish any current editor before opening another. Quest data affects both new and ongoing adventures, so verify prerequisites, task progression, quest-giver references, and rewards before saving. Test the resulting quest with an appropriate character.

entries.name: Raid
paragraphs: `RAID` opens the raid selection interaction when the raid service is available. The menu identifies the race and other choices, and the command checks the required payment and whether another raid is already in progress.

Raids are currently disabled for characters below level 103. Staff who can access the interaction should check its current state and coordinate before starting an event. A missing selector or an active raid can prevent a new one from starting.

entries.name: Test
paragraphs: `TEST` is a staff diagnostic dispatcher used during development. Its available subcommands depend on the current test script; it is not a player skill or a general testing tutorial.

Use only a diagnostic whose current behavior you have reviewed. Some tests change world or character state, while others only print measurements. Coordinate any live-server use and prefer a local game for experiments. For ordinary combat probability testing, use the documented `TESTROLL` command.

entries.name: Account
paragraphs: `ACCOUNT` displays the items in your storage account when used at a banker who offers item storage. Each stored item is listed with a number, followed by your remaining storage slots.

To retrieve an item, use `COLLECT` and its current list number. Use `STORAGE` at the banker for instructions and `OFFER <ITEM>` to ask about storing something you are carrying. This account is item storage, not your coin balance or website login.

entries.name: Allow
paragraphs: `ALLOW` toggles another player's permission to enter your manor. Use it within your property and name an existing player.

If the player is already allowed, the same command revokes their access. Only the owner may change these permissions. Review `REPORT` afterwards to confirm the current list, and take care not to repeat the command unintentionally.

entries.name: Assault
paragraphs: `ASSAULT PEDESTAL` attacks a pedestal during the event that provides that objective. It works only at an eligible pedestal, not on arbitrary scenery or characters.

Follow the event's instructions and remain at the objective while the attempt runs. The pedestal and current event state determine whether the assault can proceed. Use ordinary combat commands when you intend to fight a creature instead.

entries.name: Barrage
paragraphs: `BARRAGE` uses a suitable wielded bow to send repeated arrows into an area in the chosen direction. You must know both the bow skill and Barrage, be standing, and be out of melee combat.

You need an appropriate outdoor firing position and target area; roofs and unsuitable exits prevent the attack. This is an area technique rather than a shot at one named opponent. Read the firing messages and stop or reposition if the situation changes.

entries.name: Blast
paragraphs: `BLAST` fires an equipped shocklance at a visible target in your room. With no name, an eligible current opponent can be used.
This action belongs to that special weapon. Ordinary weapons do not gain a ranged attack from the command. Peaceful rooms prevent its use; follow the weapon's messages for any other requirements.

entries.name: Blow
paragraphs: `BLOW HORN` sounds a suitable warning horn. At the location where that horn is provided, it can announce an alarm to the surrounding area.

The horn must support the interaction and be available to you. This is not a universal command for every decorative horn. Use the room or item description to identify the intended object before sounding an alarm.

entries.name: Browse
paragraphs: `BROWSE` requests information from a vendor that supports browsing, such as a recipe seller, crafting merchant, or feat-point shop.

Begin with `BROWSE` alone, then follow that merchant's menu or selection instructions. Browsing does not by itself buy an item. Available stock, prices, and access depend on the vendor and your character; ordinary shops may use `LIST` instead.

entries.name: Claim
paragraphs: `CLAIM` attempts to take ownership of a manor when used at its claim location near the flag. It is a property action, not a command for picking up items.

The manor's ownership and current conditions determine whether you may begin. A contested claim can alert defenders and requires time to complete. Follow the messages during the attempt; do not assume ownership has changed until it confirms success. Owners can use `REPORT` to review their property.

entries.name: Climb
paragraphs: `CLIMB` attempts to scale a climbable feature in your room. Use the keyword given by its description, such as a ladder or tree.

The feature determines the route and requirements. Some climbs take time, can fail, or can cause a fall. Mounted or fighting characters may be unable to climb. It only works where a climbing interaction is provided.

entries.name: Collect
paragraphs: `COLLECT` retrieves an item from your storage account at a banker who provides item storage. First use `ACCOUNT` to obtain the current numbered list.

The number identifies the stored item; it is not a quantity or an object vnum. Check the list again after collecting something because the remaining numbers may change. Allow the banker to finish returning the item before making another request.

entries.name: Crawl
paragraphs: `CRAWL` travels through a low passage where the room provides that interaction, including the crawl entrance and exit in the Baerlon mines.
Read the room description to confirm where the passage leads. This command does not create a crawling posture that works in every room; it uses the particular route available at that location.

entries.name: Cut
paragraphs: `CUT ROPE` cuts a rope at a location or encounter that supports the action. It can free something restrained by that rope and advance the associated interaction.

The command is not a general way to damage every rope, item, or character. Identify the rope from the encounter's description and follow its requirements. Once a rope has been cut, repeating the action may have nothing left to do.

entries.name: Deliver
paragraphs: `DELIVER` completes a scripted handover when the relevant quest recipient and delivery are ready. The package or orders may be recorded in your quest inventory rather than carried as an ordinary object.

Go to the recipient described in your journal and follow the quest's instructions. The command checks the appropriate quest stage and item; it is not a substitute for every use of `GIVE`. Wait for the recipient's response and then check your journal.

entries.name: Dismiss
paragraphs: `DISMISS` requests departure through certain guarded clan entrances. A guard or room interaction opens the appropriate route or moves you outside when you are permitted to leave that way.

It is not a general command for removing followers or expelling other players. Availability depends on the entrance, your clan, and the guard's instructions. Use `UNGROUP` or `FOLLOW SELF` for ordinary party changes.

entries.name: Drag
paragraphs: `DRAG` takes hold of a movable quest or ammunition crate so it can be hauled along with you. The crate must support dragging, and you may need the corresponding quest to be active.

A crate already being dragged by someone else cannot simply be taken over, and you may be limited to one at a time. Use `RELEASE <CRATE>` when you want to let go. This does not turn ordinary containers into movable quest crates.

entries.name: Dump
paragraphs: `DUMP CORPSE` disposes of the quest-related corpse at the location designated by the adventure. The relevant quest must be at the correct stage and the expected corpse must be available.

This is a special disposal action, not a way to empty every container. Read your journal and the room description before using it. For an ordinary carried item, `DROP` is the usual command for leaving it on the ground.

entries.name: Dust
paragraphs: `DUST` performs dusting work where the White Tower chore interactions are available. Use the appropriate cleaning implement and follow the instructions for that chore.

The work uses movement and takes time. Trying again too quickly or while exhausted prevents progress. Rewards and eligibility depend on your character and the task; dusting an arbitrary room does not automatically earn credit.

entries.name: Fence
paragraphs: `FENCE` offers the stolen quest item expected by a fence who supports that interaction. The recipient checks your quest inventory automatically; you do not name an item after the command. The item and quest stage must match what the recipient expects.

This is not the ordinary shop-selling command. Trading stolen goods can have consequences depending on the recipient and encounter, so pay attention to the dialogue and your journal. Use `SELL` for normal transactions at a shop.

entries.name: Flip
paragraphs: `FLIP HOURGLASS` turns the special hourglass involved in its associated quest. At the correct quest stage, turning it can trigger the next part of the encounter, including a change of location.
This item action is separate from any social use of the word flip. Read the quest instructions and make sure you are ready to proceed before turning the hourglass.

entries.name: Grind
paragraphs: `GRIND` works with the special mortar and pestle used for grinding ingredients. Hold the mortar and place one supported ingredient inside before using the command.

The current interaction supports only a limited ingredient conversion, not every herb or recipe. An empty mortar, multiple ingredients, or an unsupported ingredient will not produce the intended result. Successful grinding consumes the input. `MIX` is a separate process using a vial.

entries.name: Hammer
paragraphs: `HAMMER` is one of the sledgehammer actions used during the Hindering Blockade quest. You need the quest at the appropriate stage and the required sledgehammer in your inventory or equipment.

Use the direction indicated by the encounter. The work takes several swings, so allow each timed stage to finish. This is a quest interaction rather than a general command for destroying doors or walls.

entries.name: Pound
paragraphs: `POUND` is one of the sledgehammer actions used during the Hindering Blockade quest. You need the quest at the appropriate stage and the required sledgehammer in your inventory or equipment.

Use the direction indicated by the encounter. The work takes several swings, so allow each timed stage to finish. This is a quest interaction rather than a general command for destroying doors or walls.

entries.name: Sledge
paragraphs: `SLEDGE` is one of the sledgehammer actions used during the Hindering Blockade quest. You need the quest at the appropriate stage and the required sledgehammer in your inventory or equipment.

Use the direction indicated by the encounter. The work takes several swings, so allow each timed stage to finish. This is a quest interaction rather than a general command for destroying doors or walls.

entries.name: Hitch
paragraphs: `HITCH` attaches a suitable cart to a mount in your room. Name the cart first and the mount second; do not insert the word "to" between them.

You must be on the ground, standing and out of combat, and not riding. The cart must support hitching and the mount must be available. A mount cannot pull two carts at once. Use `UNHITCH` to detach the cart.

entries.name: Inspect
paragraphs: `INSPECT` examines a particular quest feature that provides a closer-inspection interaction, such as a well or an embedded object.

The resulting information may be a puzzle, a clue, or progress in an encounter. The feature must be present and your quest may need to be at the right stage. Use `EXAMINE` for ordinary item inspection.

entries.name: Invite
paragraphs: `INVITE` admits another player through certain private or clan entrances. Name the player and include `INSIDE` when the entrance asks for that form.

You must be authorized to use that particular entrance, and the person must be in the location expected by its guard. This is not a universal group invitation. Manor permission uses `ALLOW`, while travelling parties use `FOLLOW` and `GROUP`.

entries.name: Jump
paragraphs: `JUMP` attempts the special crossing or leap available in your current room. It is used at certain ledges and other scripted obstacles.

The landing, timing, and risk depend on the location. A failed jump can cause injury or leave you somewhere dangerous, so read the room description before attempting it. Typing `JUMP` in an ordinary room does not move you through a normal exit.

entries.name: Leap
paragraphs: `LEAP` takes the special leap provided by an encounter, including the descent into the ravine where that action is described.

This is a location-specific movement action. The descent can injure you, and the landing may not offer an immediate return route. Check your condition and the room description before committing to it.

entries.name: Learn
paragraphs: `LEARN` adds an eligible recipe parchment from your inventory to your recipe book. The parchment must be the recipe you name and must be ready to learn.

Once learned, the recipe is recorded for use through `RECIPES`. Fragments may first need to be joined with `COMBINE`. Learning a recipe is separate from increasing the associated trade skill, which requires training and practice.

entries.name: Load
paragraphs: `LOAD` puts a suitable cannonball from your inventory into a ship's cannon. Supply the ammunition keyword followed by the cannon keyword.

The cannon must be empty and both items must support this interaction. Loading takes time, and a mishap can drop the ball or hurt someone nearby. Once loaded, use `SHOOT CANNON` when the ship is in a suitable firing position. This command does not create objects.

entries.name: Lower
paragraphs: `LOWER ANCHOR` lowers the anchor of the ship where this interaction is available. Use the complete two-word command.

Lowering an anchor takes time and changes the ship's anchored state. An already lowered anchor cannot be lowered again. Coordinate with the person steering; use `RAISE ANCHOR` to lift it before continuing the journey.

entries.name: Make
paragraphs: `MAKE SANDWICH` prepares a sandwich at the kitchen that provides this action. The preparation takes time and must complete successfully before the food appears.

This is a kitchen-specific interaction, not a universal crafting command. Other crafting systems use their own commands and requirements, such as `TAILOR` or `MIX`. Follow the room's instructions for what can be prepared there.

entries.name: Paint
paragraphs: `PAINT GATES` performs the painting task in the associated quest. You must have the required quest supplies, be at the correct gates, and be ready for that stage of the adventure.
The command does not recolor arbitrary objects or rooms. Follow the quest giver's directions, allow the action to finish, and review your journal for progress afterwards.

entries.name: Pass
paragraphs: `PASS` throws the special football to a visible player in your room. You need the football involved in that interaction.
A pass can be fumbled, so the ball may not arrive as intended. This is an item action rather than a generic transfer command; use `GIVE` to hand over an ordinary object without a football pass.

entries.name: Place
paragraphs: `PLACE` puts a quest item where an encounter expects it. Depending on the task, this can mean placing an urn at a burial site or inserting a carried item into a puzzle feature.
Use the object and destination named by the quest, and make sure its stage is ready. This is not a replacement for every use of `PUT`: ordinary container storage still uses `PUT <ITEM> <CONTAINER>`.

entries.name: Play
paragraphs: `PLAY` joins the special ter'angreal game where its table or game object is available. It enrolls you during the sign-up stage; a game already in progress may not accept new players.

Read the game's rules and announcements before joining. Ter'angreal games can have dangerous consequences, and `TOUCH` can be part of taking a turn. This is not a command for starting every minigame from any room.

entries.name: Pull
paragraphs: `PULL` operates a feature that supports pulling, such as a lever, a bell rope, or an interactive item. Use the feature's keyword and follow any direction or position requested by the encounter.
Pulling can open or close a passage, sound a signal, or trigger a quest response. Some mechanisms require time or strength. It is not a general way to drag ordinary items; quest crates use `DRAG`.

entries.name: Push
paragraphs: `PUSH` operates a pushable feature in a supported encounter. Examples include an Arena boulder and certain buttons or interactive objects.

The feature decides the required position, effort, and outcome. Pushing may move an obstacle or activate a mechanism; it does not generally move every object in the room. Read the description before pressing an unfamiliar control.

entries.name: Raise
paragraphs: `RAISE ANCHOR` lifts the anchor on a ship that supports this interaction. Use the complete command while at the ship's anchor.
The work takes time and must complete before the anchored state changes. Coordinate with the crew so the ship is ready to move. Use `LOWER ANCHOR` when you need to anchor it again.

entries.name: Rake
paragraphs: `RAKE` performs the garden-raking chore where that task is available. You need the appropriate implement, a garden that still needs work, and enough movement to carry it out.

The chore checks your position and eligibility. Work at the pace described by the messages; repeating the command too quickly does not speed it up. Rewards depend on the chore and your character, and a clean area has nothing further to rake.

entries.name: Ring
paragraphs: `RING BELL` sounds an interactive city bell at its location. The alarm may be heard beyond the room, so use it with a purpose.
The bell must provide the ringing interaction. This does not activate every item with "bell" in its name. Look at the room for the appropriate feature and pay attention to the response.

entries.name: Steer
paragraphs: `STEER` changes the heading of the ship whose steering wheel you are operating. Specify one of the four compass directions.

Turning the wheel affects that ship, not your character's normal movement. The ship must be in a state where steering can complete. Coordinate with the crew and the anchor operator before changing course.

entries.name: Storage
paragraphs: `STORAGE` asks a banker who handles item storage for instructions. That service stores eligible items for a fee, shows them with `ACCOUNT`, and returns them with `COLLECT <NUMBER>`.

Ask for a price with `OFFER <ITEM>` before handing over an item. Storage slots and eligibility are limited. At a crafting merchant, `STORAGE` can instead display your stored crafting materials; follow that merchant's withdrawal instructions.

entries.name: Touch
paragraphs: `TOUCH` interacts with the special ter'angreal used by the game at that location. Name the visible game object you intend to touch.

Touching it can commit a game action with dangerous consequences. Follow the rules and wait for your turn rather than experimenting during another player's action. The command is not a universal activation method for every ter'angreal or ordinary object.

entries.name: Trim
paragraphs: `TRIM HEDGES` carries out the hedge-trimming task where that encounter is available. You need the required garden shears in your inventory and hedges that still need the work.

Trimming takes several stages. Let each stage finish; interruption can stop the job before you receive completion credit. Once the hedges are properly trimmed, the same quest task cannot simply be repeated for more credit.

entries.name: Unfold
paragraphs: `UNFOLD` opens the special folded paper involved in its quest. Carry the paper and identify it by one of its keywords.

Unfolding reveals the message and may record the item or clue in your journal. The relevant quest must permit that action. It does not unfold every ordinary item; use `READ` or `EXAMINE` for other written material.

entries.name: Unhitch
paragraphs: `UNHITCH` detaches a supported cart from a mount. Name the cart and then the mount, without the word "from" between them.

You must be standing on the ground, out of combat, and not riding. The cart and mount must be present and match the hitching interaction. Check that the cart is safely where you want it before moving on.

entries.name: Wash
paragraphs: `WASH DISHES` performs the dishwashing chore in the kitchen where it is provided. There must be dirty dishes available, and you need the appropriate position, energy, and eligibility for the task.

Allow the work to finish and follow its pace; rushing can interrupt the chore. A room with no dishes or an already clean set offers nothing to wash. This is a chore interaction, not a general equipment-cleaning command.
